beats.title: Set ∠ABP to 40° and trace the angle chain
beats.instruction: Two horizontal parallel lines are cut by a transversal through B. Drag point P to set ∠ABP to 40°. When the angle is correct, observe how every other angle in the figure is determined by parallel-line theorems.
beats.successMessage: With ∠ABP = 40°, you can find every other angle in the figure using parallel line theorems.

beats.title: Find all angles given one angle measure

steps.text: Given m∠2 = 115°. ∠1 and ∠2 are a linear pair at E (they share ray EF and together form the straight line p), so they are supplementary: m∠1 = 180° − 115° = 65°.
Vertical angles at E: ∠3 (lower-left at E, on the same side as ∠1 but below line p) is vertical to ∠1, so m∠3 = 65°. ∠4 (lower-right at E) is vertical to ∠2, so m∠4 = 115°.
Since p ∥ q, apply the Corresponding Angles Theorem: ∠5 at F (upper-right, same position as ∠1 at E) equals ∠1, so m∠5 = 65°. Similarly m∠6 = 115°, m∠7 = 65°, m∠8 = 115°.

Cross-check with other theorems. Alternate interior angles: ∠4 (lower-right at E) and ∠5 (upper-right at F) are on opposite sides of the transversal, between the lines — both should be equal. But ∠4 = 115° and ∠5 = 65°. Wait — ∠4 is lower-right at E (same side as the transversal direction toward F) and ∠5 is upper-right at F. The alternate interior pair is actually ∠3 (lower-left at E) and ∠5 (upper-right at F): m∠3 = 65° = m∠5 ✓. Co-interior angles: ∠4 (lower-right at E) and ∠5 (upper-right at F) are on the same side — m∠4 + m∠5 = 115° + 65° = 180° ✓. All relationships confirmed.

items.prompt: In a figure with two parallel lines cut by a transversal, angle X is between the parallel lines on the left side of the transversal. Angle Y is between the parallel lines on the right side of the transversal at the other parallel line. What is the relationship between ∠X and ∠Y?
choices: They are corresponding angles and are equal.
They are alternate interior angles and are equal.
They are co-interior angles and sum to 180°.
They are vertical angles and are equal.
items.explanation: Both angles are between the parallel lines (interior) and on opposite sides of the transversal (alternate) — making them alternate interior angles, which are congruent when the lines are parallel.

items.prompt: Parallel lines p and q are cut by transversal t. An angle at intersection E on line p measures 70°. How many of the eight angles formed by t with p and q equal 70°?
items.explanation: At each intersection, opposite angles are equal (vertical angles). At E, the 70° angle and its vertical angle equal 70° — that's 2 at E. By corresponding or alternate interior angles, the equivalent pair at the intersection on q also measures 70° — that's 2 more. Total: 4 angles equal 70°, and the other 4 equal 110°.

items.prompt: Parallel lines m and n are cut by a transversal. At the intersection on m, one angle is 73°. Find the co-interior angle at n on the same side of the transversal.
hints: Co-interior (same-side interior) angles between parallel lines are supplementary.

items.prompt: Parallel lines j and k are cut by transversal t. At j, one angle in the figure is 48°. A student needs the alternate exterior angle at k. What is it?
hints: Alternate exterior angles between parallel lines are congruent.
The alternate exterior angle equals the given angle.

items.prompt: Parallel lines a and b are cut by transversal t. An angle at a measures 55°. Which set of angles at b also measure 55°?
choices: The co-interior angle and the alternate exterior angle on the same side.
The corresponding angle and the alternate interior angle.
The corresponding angle and the co-interior angle.
items.explanation: Corresponding angles are equal (both 55°). Alternate interior angles are also equal to the corresponding angle's vertical partner, which is 55°. Co-interior angles sum to 180° and would be 125°, not 55°.

items.prompt: Parallel lines p and q are cut by transversal t. At p, two adjacent angles are (3x + 5)° and (x + 15)°. These two angles form a linear pair. Find x, then find the measure of the larger angle.
hints: Angles: 3(40) + 5 = 125° and 40 + 15 = 55°. Check: 125 + 55 = 180 ✓. The larger angle is 125°.

testItems.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle in the figure is 62°. What is the measure of the vertical angle to this 62° angle?
Parallel lines p and q are cut by a transversal. An angle at p measures 83°. Find the supplement of its corresponding angle at q.
Parallel lines r and s are cut by a transversal. The co-interior angles on the left side of the transversal are (2x + 10)° and (3x − 5)°. Find x.
In a figure with two parallel lines and a transversal, which two angles at a single intersection are always supplementary but not vertical?
choices: A linear pair (adjacent angles on a straight line).
testItems.explanation: Vertical angles are equal, not supplementary (unless both are 90°). Corresponding and alternate interior angles involve angles at different intersections. A linear pair at one intersection are adjacent and supplementary.

testItems.prompt: Parallel lines a and b are cut by transversal t. At intersection E on a, angle ∠1 = (5x − 20)°. At intersection F on b, the alternate interior angle ∠2 = (3x + 16)°. Find m∠1.
testItems.explanation: Alternate interior angles are equal: 5x − 20 = 3x + 16 → 2x = 36 → x = 18. m∠1 = 5(18) − 20 = 70°. Check: 3(18) + 16 = 70° ✓.

testItems.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle is (4x + 9)°. Its co-interior partner is (2x + 51)°. Find the measure of the larger co-interior angle.
testItems.explanation: Co-interior angles sum to 180°: (4x + 9) + (2x + 51) = 180 → 6x + 60 = 180 → x = 20. Angles: 89° and 91°. Larger = 91°.

testItems.prompt: Three parallel lines are cut by a single transversal. How many distinct angle measures can appear in the figure (ignoring which specific angles have each measure)?
testItems.explanation: At each intersection a transversal creates two supplementary angle pairs: one acute measure α and its supplement 180° − α. All intersections with parallel lines produce the same two measures. So only 2 distinct measures appear regardless of how many parallel lines there are.
